purpose: Atomic replacement of one pending Shine Defence review candidate by one newer pending candidate for the same app.
successor: The successor object is the same bounded candidate-intake payload accepted by candidate-intake-v1.
preconditions: The superseded candidate exists exactly once and is pending_review.
The old candidate has no final review decision.

If the old candidate has a canonical checklist, humanAuthorization must still be pending; an approved or rejected human decision must be finalized through its matching acceptance or rejection path instead.
The successor belongs to the same app, repository and profile path as the old candidate.
The successor release identity differs from the old candidate and passes the canonical candidate-intake validator.
The successor observedAt timestamp is not earlier than the old candidate observedAt timestamp.
The supersededAt timestamp is not earlier than either candidate observation timestamp.
atomicState: The old candidate becomes superseded and records supersededByCandidateId equal to the deterministic successor candidate id.
Exactly one superseded review decision is appended for the old candidate and names the same successor candidate id.
The successor is appended as the app's only pending_review candidate.
If the old candidate already has a canonical checklist, the superseded decision pins its exact checklist Git blob and checklist registry identity.
boundaries: Supersession does not certify either candidate.
Supersession does not change the reviewed ecosystem ledger, certification receipts or revocations.
Supersession does not delete an old checklist or advisory evidence suggestions; if present, they become fingerprint-locked historical review assistance.
The successor starts with no checklist authorization and must proceed through the normal structured-review workflow.
atomicity: The candidate queue and review-decision ledger are one guarded repository transition.
Apply mode validates the complete resulting Defence state and restores both files if any gate fails.
At no valid repository state may the same app have two pending_review candidates.
nonClaims: Superseded does not mean rejected or unsafe.
The supersession authority is operational provenance, not certification authority.
A newer candidate does not inherit checklist findings or human authorization from the superseded candidate.
